#The look of the browser's own interface

The tab bar, the tabs, the toolbar and the address field are drawn by the toolkit (not by a page). Two styles, chosen by a preference, and a palette on top of either (browser.ui.theme: Graphite, Daylight, Nord, ...).

PreferenceDefault
browser.ui.chrome_styleclassicmodern: flat, tabs are rounded pills. classic: Chrome of 2010-2015, see below. Applies at once.
browser.ui.classic_slope_deg22Classic: how far the sides of a tab lean from the vertical (8 to 40). The larger, the more angular, the more the tabs overlap.
browser.ui.classic_gloss1Classic: strength of the gradients and of the steps between the current tab, the other tabs and the tab bar (0 = flat colors, shapes and lines stay; 2 = more depth).

Change it in about:config, with wren ctl pref set browser.ui.chrome_style modern, from the command palette (Appearance: classic tabs, Appearance: modern tabs) or from the menu, View.

#Classic

  • Tabs are trapezoids: sloped sides, rounded shoulders, and at each foot a concave curve that flares out and joins the toolbar's line, as a fillet. A thin dark line runs outside the shape and a light one inside, along the top and the sides.
  • The current tab is attached to the toolbar: its gradient goes on into the toolbar's, and the toolbar's top line is interrupted under it (between the two curves of its feet): no line between them. The other tabs are lower in value (darker on a light palette, and on a dark one), have their own gradient, sit behind the current one and overlap by a few pixels (their feet are covered by the next tab). Under the pointer a tab is lit most of the way to the current one.
  • Gradients on the tab bar (a little lighter at the top), on every tab, on the toolbar, and in the address field, which is a white (dark palettes: darker than the toolbar) hollow with an outline and a light line under it.
  • Title cut by a fade, not dots; a close cross on every tab that is wide enough (browser.tabs.close_button_min_em), the loading indicator, the icon, drag to reorder, scrolling when the tabs are too many, the new-tab button (a faint small trapezoid) work as in the modern style.
  • A dragged tab is drawn on top, with a shadow.

#Classic, with the tabs in a sidebar

browser.tabs.position = left | right (tab-sidebar.md): the same family turned on its side.

  • The sidebar is the tab bar: its gradient runs from the outer edge (lighter) toward the page (darker), and the dark line of the tab bar's edge runs along its inner edge. With an integrated title bar, the toolbar is the title bar (tab-sidebar.md, "The toolbar in the title bar"): the toolbar's gradient and its bottom line, no line along its top (the window's edge), the classic address field. With the system's title bar, the toolbar is the classic one under it, its top line whole.
  • The current tab is a classic tab with upright sides (slope 0) lying across its row: rounded shoulders on the outer side, concave feet that flare into the inner edge's line above and below the row and interrupt it, the body flowing on into the page's side, as the top's current tab flows into the toolbar. Lit from above, like the toolbar (the current tab's colors, top to bottom of the row). Left and right are mirrors: the rounded side is always the outer one.
  • The other tabs lie flat on the bar, engraved apart (a dark and a light hairline, clear of both ends; none next to the current tab or to the one under the pointer). Under the pointer: a rounded panel of a classic inactive tab's colors (lighter than the bar, darker than the current tab), clear of the inner edge: it is not attached to the page.
  • Icons only (browser.tabs.sidebar_collapsed): the same shapes, narrower. The new-tab button is the "+" glyph alone, lit under the pointer like the toolbar's buttons (as in the modern style; no trapezoid). The scroll bar is on the outer side (gui_toolkit's Box_Flag.Scrollbar_Left for a left sidebar): the inner edge belongs to the current tab.
  • The shape is the top's (tab_shape_get, the same cache), moved to the screen by side_point (the tab's axes are the row's: along the tab is down, its top to its foot is the outer side to the inner edge). The current row is built after the others (its feet flare over its neighbours' rows); the rows are not clipped, the list is.
  • Tests (chrome_style_test.odin): side_tab_lies_across_its_row (rounded corners on the outer side, open on the inner edge, feet's flare, left and right mirrored), side_colors_compose_with_palettes, classic_on_follows_the_style_at_every_position.

#How the colors are made

No palette is named: from the palette's window color base and border, shade(base, amount) is a mix toward white or black in sRGB values (the way the toolkit steps its hover and press states), by amounts that depend on whether the palette is light or dark (average sRGB value of base under one half). classic_gloss scales the amounts. See classic_colors in src/browser/chrome_style.odin; chrome_style_test.odin checks the order tab bar < other tabs < current tab on every named palette.

#How it is drawn, and clicked

  • A tab is three polygons (the region under its outline moved out by a hairline, as is, moved in by a hairline) used as the toolkit's polygon clip: a flat dark fill, a flat light fill, then the gradient. Hairlines are whole physical pixels, and every length is in em or in dpi units, so lines stay sharp at 100, 125, 150 and 175 %.
  • The shapes are made once per size in the tab's own coordinates (tab_shape_get: a small cache) and only moved when drawn: a frame that draws the strip again makes no geometry. Nothing draws while nothing changes (the chrome is drawn when a frame is asked for, as before).
  • The hit shape of a tab is ui.Box.slant (gui_toolkit 0.28.0): the toolkit's pointer tests, and the window's hit test over an integrated title bar (platform.Chrome_Regions.slanted), follow the trapezoid: the corners a tab does not cover still drag the window. Tabs are built in the order they are drawn (the others from left to right, the current one, the one dragged), the last one under the pointer getting the click, so a click in two overlapping feet goes to the tab on top. (Consequence: the Tab key goes through the tabs in that order.)
